1.title: When I was a child
1.brief: Write an email to a new friend from another country about your childhood. Describe where you lived, what you used to do and one thing you didn't use to like.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo extranjero sobre tu infancia: dónde vivías, qué solías hacer y algo que no te gustaba.
criteria: Three affirmative “used to” sentences and one negative (didn’t use to).
Two words from the unit: childhood, back then, memory, ago.
A friendly greeting, two paragraphs and a closing.
1.model:
Hi Olivia,

You asked me about my childhood, so here it is! When I was a child, I lived on a farm near Armenia. Back then, we didn't have internet, so I used to play outside all day. My brother and I used to climb trees and we used to help my grandfather with the coffee plants.

I didn't use to like school because it was far away: I walked for an hour every morning! My best memory is the smell of coffee in the kitchen. What about you?

Hugs,
Mateo

1.title: The day everything changed
1.brief: Write a short story about a day when something surprising happened. Use the simple past to tell the events in order.
1.briefEs: Escribe una historia corta sobre un día en que pasó algo sorprendente, en pasado simple.
criteria: Eight verbs in the simple past, at least four irregular.
Use “suddenly” and “at the time”.
One sentence with “was / were” to set the scene.
1.model: It was a normal Tuesday in 2019. I was 15 and I was at school. At the time, I didn't know anything about my father's plans. When I got home, my parents were in the kitchen with a big map. Suddenly, my father said, “We're moving to Canada!” I didn't believe him. I cried and I called my best friend. Two months later, we took a plane to Toronto. That day changed my life, and now I'm happy it happened.

1.title: A social media post: then and now
1.brief: Write a post for social media with an old photo. Compare how things used to be and how they are now.
1.briefEs: Escribe una publicación para redes con una foto antigua comparando cómo eran las cosas y cómo son ahora.
criteria: Two “used to” sentences and two present simple sentences.
Use “ago” correctly (ten years ago).
Include “to quit” or “to move (house)”.
1.model: #ThrowbackThursday This photo is from fifteen years ago! I used to have very long hair and I used to wear huge glasses. I used to play the violin, but I quit when I was twelve. We used to live in Cúcuta, but we moved house to Bogotá in 2015. Now I have short hair and I wear contact lenses. I don't play the violin anymore, but I sing in a choir. Do you remember me like this?

2.title: Shopping list for a party
2.brief: You are organising a party with a roommate. Write a message saying what you have, what you need and how much or how many.
2.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a tu compañero de cuarto sobre lo que tienen y lo que falta para una fiesta.
criteria: Use “a few / a little / a lot of / plenty of” correctly with count and noncount nouns.
Use “enough” and “not enough” once each.
Use “run out of” once.
2.model: Hi Juli! I checked the kitchen for the party. We have plenty of glasses and a lot of plates, but we don't have enough chairs. There's a little rice but not enough for twenty people, so please buy two kilos. We've run out of sugar and we only have a few lemons. There isn't much ice either. Can you buy a couple of bags? I'll buy the drinks and a few snacks.

2.title: Asking politely at a hotel
2.brief: Write an email to a hotel before your trip. Ask for information using indirect questions.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un hotel pidiendo información con preguntas indirectas.
criteria: Four indirect questions (Could you tell me…? I'd like to know…).
Statement word order inside each question (where the station is).
Use “whether” or “if” once.
2.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am planning to stay at your hotel from 12 to 15 May. Could you tell me how much a double room costs? I would like to know whether breakfast is included. I was wondering if you have a room with a view of the sea. Do you know how far the hotel is from the airport? Could you also tell me what time check-in is?

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Paola Herrera

2.title: What's in my fridge
2.brief: Describe what is in your fridge and kitchen today. Say what you have a lot of, a little of and what you need to buy.
2.briefEs: Describe qué hay hoy en tu nevera y cocina, y qué necesitas comprar.
criteria: Five different expressions of quantity.
No plural for noncount nouns (no “breads”, “milks”).
Use “container”, “quantity” or “a couple of”.
2.model: My fridge is almost empty today! There is a little milk and a couple of eggs. There are a few tomatoes, but there isn't any cheese. I have a big container of soup from yesterday — plenty for two people. In the cupboard there is a lot of rice and some pasta, but there isn't much coffee. I need to buy fruit, bread and more coffee. I can't live without coffee!

3.title: My flat: good and bad
3.brief: Describe your home. Evaluate it with adjectives and nouns (too small, not big enough, enough space) and say what you wish was different.
3.briefEs: Describe tu vivienda evaluándola (too, enough) y di qué desearías que fuera diferente.
criteria: Use “too + adjective” and “not + adjective + enough”.
Use “enough + noun” once.
Two wishes with “I wish + past simple / could”.
3.model: I live in a small flat in Medellín. It's very convenient because it's near the metro, but it's too noisy at night. The kitchen isn't big enough for a table, and there isn't enough space for my bike. On the good side, the rent is decent and the neighbours are friendly. I wish I had a balcony with plants. I wish the walls were thicker! And I wish I could have a dog, but the building doesn't allow pets.

3.title: A complaint about a hostel
3.brief: Write an online review of a place you didn't like (a hostel, a restaurant, a gym). Explain the drawbacks.
3.briefEs: Escribe una reseña en línea de un lugar que no te gustó y explica sus desventajas.
criteria: Three evaluations with too / enough / as… as.
Use “to complain”, “drawback” and “crowded”.
One wish about the place.
3.model:
Hostel Sol, Cartagena ★★
I stayed here for three nights and I have to complain. The location is great, but that's the only good thing. The rooms are too small and too hot, and there aren't enough fans. The bathroom isn't as clean as the photos show. The biggest drawback is the noise: the bar is very crowded until 2 a.m. I wish the staff were more helpful. I put up with it because it was cheap, but I won't go back.

3.title: If only…
3.brief: Write about three things in your life that you would like to change. Use wishes and explain why.
3.briefEs: Escribe tres cosas de tu vida que te gustaría cambiar usando “I wish” y explica por qué.
criteria: Three wishes with “I wish + past simple” or “could”.
Use “because” to give a reason for each wish.
Use one phrasal expression: put up with, settle for.
3.model: I'm quite happy, but there are three things I wish were different. First, I wish I lived closer to work because I spend two hours on the bus every day. Second, I wish I could speak English fluently, because I want to travel. Third, I wish my brother didn't play loud music: I have to put up with it every night! For now, I settle for headphones and patience.

4.title: How I learned to cook
4.brief: Tell the story of how you learned something (to cook, to drive, to swim). Use sequence adverbs to order the steps.
4.briefEs: Cuenta cómo aprendiste algo (cocinar, manejar, nadar) usando adverbios de secuencia.
criteria: Use first, then, after that, next and finally.
The story is in the simple past.
One closing sentence in the present perfect (Since then, I have…).
4.model: I learned to cook when I was 18. First, my grandmother taught me to make rice. It was a disaster! Then I tried simple things like eggs and soup. After that, I looked up recipes online and practised every weekend. Next, I cooked a full lunch for my family on my mom's birthday. Finally, my grandmother said, “Now you are a real cook.” Since then, I have cooked hundreds of meals, and I have never burnt the rice again.

4.title: My experiences so far
4.brief: Write an email to a friend about your first month in a new job or course. Say what you have done so far and what you haven't done yet.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre tu primer mes en un trabajo o curso: lo que has hecho y lo que aún no.
criteria: Four sentences in the present perfect with so far, already, yet, recently.
One sentence in the simple past with a finished time (last Monday).
Use “since” or “for” once.
4.model:
Hi Manu,

I've been at my new job for a month now and I love it! So far, I have met all my team and I have already finished my first project. Recently, I have started to take the bike to work. Last Monday I gave my first presentation. I was nervous, but it went well. I haven't met the big boss yet and I haven't got my first salary yet!

Write soon,
Isa

4.title: A biography in steps
4.brief: Write a short biography of a famous Colombian or a member of your family. Say what they achieved, in order.
4.briefEs: Escribe una biografía corta de un colombiano famoso o un familiar, contando sus logros en orden.
criteria: Simple past for finished events with dates.
Present perfect for life achievements up to now (has won, has written).
Three sequence adverbs.
4.model: Mariana Pajón is a famous Colombian BMX rider. She was born in Medellín in 1991. First, she started riding bikes when she was four. Then she won her first world championship as a teenager. After that, she won a gold medal at the London Olympics in 2012, and she won another one in Rio in 2016. Next, she got silver in Tokyo. Up to now, she has won more than ten world titles and she has become a role model for many young athletes.

5.title: My plans and predictions
5.brief: Write about your plans for next year and make two predictions about your country or your city.
5.briefEs: Escribe sobre tus planes del próximo año y haz dos predicciones sobre tu país o ciudad.
criteria: Three plans with “be going to”.
Two predictions with “will” or “won’t”.
Use “be likely to” once.
5.model: Next year is going to be very important for me. I'm going to finish my degree in June, and I'm going to look for a job in a tech company. I'm also going to take an English exam. About my city, I think the new metro line will be ready, so traffic won't be so bad. Prices are likely to go up, unfortunately. I think more tourists will come to Bogotá because it's becoming very popular.

5.title: Advice before an exam
5.brief: A friend has an important exam next week. Write an email with advice using modals of necessity and suggestion.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo con consejos antes de un examen usando modales de necesidad y sugerencia.
criteria: Use must, have to, should and had better.
One negative: don’t have to or mustn’t.
Include “deadline”, “to postpone” or “to warn”.
5.model:
Hi Toño,

Your exam is next Tuesday, right? Here's my advice. You have to sleep well the night before — no parties! You should review your notes every day this week. You'd better start today because you mustn't leave everything for Monday. You don't have to study ten hours: two hours a day is enough. And I warn you, don't postpone the registration: the deadline is Friday!

Good luck!
Vale

5.title: Team plan for an event
5.brief: You are in charge of a small event at work or school. Write an email to the team with the plan: who is going to do what, what will happen and what is necessary.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo al equipo con el plan de un evento: quién hará qué y qué es necesario.
criteria: Use “be going to” for decisions already made.
Use “will” for an offer or promise (I’ll send…).
Two modals of necessity (need to, have to, must).
5.model:
Hi team,

I'm in charge of the end-of-year event, so here's the plan. Andrés is going to book the room and Lina is going to order the food. The event is going to start at 6 p.m. We have to finish the decoration by 5:00, and everybody needs to bring one thing for the raffle. It's urgent: we must confirm the number of guests by Wednesday. I'll send the invitations tomorrow. We'd better have a backup plan in case it rains.

Thanks!
Daniela

6.title: Notes for the house-sitter
6.brief: Your friend is staying at your house while you are away. Write a note asking him or her to do several things with two-part verbs.
6.briefEs: Escribe una nota para la persona que cuida tu casa pidiéndole cosas con verbos de dos partes.
criteria: Five two-part verbs (turn off, pick up, put away, look after, fill in).
Correct position of the pronoun: turn it off, not turn off it.
Use “Could you…?” or “Would you mind…?” at least twice.
6.model: Hi Simón, thanks for looking after my house! Here are a few things. Could you water the plants every two days? Please feed the cat and look after her — she's very shy. Would you mind picking up my letters? Just put them on my desk. When you leave, please turn off the lights and turn them off in the garden too. Could you put away the dishes after you use them? If the gas man comes, please fill in the form for me. Thanks a million!

6.title: Replying to a request
6.brief: A colleague sent you three requests. Write a reply accepting two and refusing one politely.
6.briefEs: Responde a un colega aceptando dos de sus peticiones y rechazando una con cortesía.
criteria: Use “I’ll…” to accept requests.
Use “I’m afraid…” to refuse politely, with a reason.
Two expressions: right away, sort out, get back to you.
6.model:
Hi Claudia,

No problem, I'll send you the report right away. I'll also call the client and sort out the problem with the invoice. I'm afraid I can't go to the meeting on Friday because I have a doctor's appointment. Could you take notes for me? I'll get back to you on Monday with my comments.

Best,
Ricardo

6.title: A favour from a teacher
6.brief: Write an email to a teacher asking for two favours (e.g. more time for homework, a letter of recommendation). Be polite.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un profesor pidiendo dos favores con mucha cortesía.
criteria: Use “Would you mind + -ing…?” once.
Use “Could you possibly…?” or “Would it be OK if…?”.
Use “to hand in” and “favour”.
6.model:
Dear Ms. Vargas,

I'm writing to ask you a favour. I was sick last week, so I couldn't finish my essay. Would you mind giving me two more days? I can hand it in on Thursday. Also, I am applying for a scholarship. Could you possibly write a short letter of recommendation for me? I understand if you are busy.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Juan Camilo Ortiz

7.title: My favourite gadget
7.brief: Describe a device you use every day. Say what it is used for and why it comes in handy.
7.briefEs: Describe un aparato que usas a diario: para qué sirve y por qué te resulta útil.
criteria: Use “is used for + -ing” and “is used to + verb”.
Use “in order to” once.
Include “device”, “tool” or “to come in handy”.
7.model: My favourite device is my e-reader. It's used for reading books, but I also use it to read articles from the internet. It's very light, so it comes in handy when I travel. I use it every night in order to relax before I sleep. It's also useful for learning English because I can touch a word to see the meaning. The battery lasts for weeks. It wasn't cheap, but it was worth every peso!

7.title: How to survive your first day
7.brief: Write tips for a new student or worker on their first day. Use imperatives and infinitives to give suggestions.
7.briefEs: Escribe consejos para el primer día de un estudiante o trabajador nuevo con imperativos e infinitivos.
criteria: Four imperatives (Arrive…, Don’t forget…).
Two suggestions with “Try to…” or “Remember to…”.
Use “to make sure” and “to avoid”.
7.model: Your first day can be stressful, so here are some tips. Arrive ten minutes early to avoid stress. Make sure you have your ID and a notebook. Don't forget to smile and introduce yourself. Try to remember people's names: write them down if necessary. Ask questions — it's normal not to know everything. Remember to bring your lunch, because the cafeteria is expensive. Finally, don't worry too much. Everyone was new once!

7.title: An instruction message
7.brief: Your grandmother has a new smartphone. Write a message explaining how to make a video call.
7.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a tu abuela explicándole cómo hacer una videollamada en su celular nuevo.
criteria: Use imperatives in the correct order with sequence words.
Use “to keep + -ing” once.
Explain the purpose of one step with “to” or “in order to”.
7.model: Hi Grandma! To make a video call, follow these steps. First, open the green app with the phone. Then find my name and touch it. After that, press the small camera icon to start the video. Keep holding the phone in front of your face so I can see you! To end the call, press the red button. Don't worry if it doesn't work the first time. Keep trying, and call me if you need help. Love you!

8.title: A turning point in my life
8.brief: Write about a moment that changed your life. Use relative clauses with “when” and time clauses with when, after and before.
8.briefEs: Escribe sobre un momento que cambió tu vida usando cláusulas con when, after y before.
criteria: One relative clause of time (the day when…, the year when…).
Two clauses with after / before / as soon as.
Use “turning point”, “to realise” or “eventually”.
8.model: 2020 was the year when everything changed for me. Before the pandemic started, I worked in a call centre and I was unhappy. When the offices closed, I had a lot of time at home. I started to bake bread while I was waiting for news. After my neighbours tried my bread, they asked me to sell it. That was the turning point. As soon as I realised I could earn money, I made a website. Eventually, I opened my own bakery.

8.title: A day of my life, in order
8.brief: Write a diary entry about a busy day. Connect the events with when, after, before, as soon as and while.
8.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario de un día ocupado conectando eventos con when, after, before, while.
criteria: Four time connectors (when, after, before, as soon as, while, until).
Use a comma when the time clause comes first.
Use “meanwhile” or “in the meantime”.
8.model: What a day! As soon as I woke up, I checked my emails. Before I had breakfast, my boss called me. While I was talking to him, the coffee burned! After I left home, I realised I didn't have my keys. I waited for my roommate until 11:00. Meanwhile, I answered messages on my phone. When I finally arrived at the office, the meeting was over. Tomorrow will be better!

8.title: Graduation memories
8.brief: Write an email to an old classmate remembering your graduation day. Describe what happened at different moments.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un excompañero recordando el día de su graduación.
criteria: Use “the day when” or “the moment when”.
Two time clauses with after / by the time / until.
Use “to graduate” and one more word from the unit.
8.model:
Hi Luisa,

Do you remember the day when we graduated? I was looking at the photos today. Before the ceremony started, we were so nervous! By the time my name was called, my hands were shaking. After we received our diplomas, we threw our hats in the air. Then we danced until the sun came up. That was the moment when I realised we were adults. I miss you!

Hugs,
Fer

9.title: My town: past, present and future
9.brief: Write a short article for a school magazine about how your town has changed and how it will be in twenty years.
9.briefEs: Escribe un artículo corto sobre cómo ha cambiado tu ciudad y cómo será en veinte años.
criteria: Use a past form (used to, was), a present form (nowadays) and a future form (will).
Include “trend” or “gradually”.
One first conditional sentence.
9.model: Zipaquirá has changed a lot. Thirty years ago, it used to be a quiet town with only a few shops. People used to travel to Bogotá by train. Nowadays, it is a popular tourist destination and there are hotels and restaurants everywhere. The population is gradually growing. In twenty years, I think it will be part of Bogotá. If the city builds a train line, people will live here and work in the capital. Unless we protect the parks, there won't be any green areas left.

9.title: If you visit my city…
9.brief: A friend is planning to visit your city. Write an email giving advice with first conditional sentences.
9.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que viene de visita con consejos usando el primer condicional.
criteria: Four first conditional sentences (If + present, will + verb).
Use “unless” and “in case” once each.
Use a comma when the if-clause comes first.
9.model:
Hi Tom,

I'm so happy you're coming to Medellín! If you arrive on a Friday, we'll go to a salsa class together. If you like coffee, I'll take you to a farm near the city. Bring an umbrella in case it rains — it usually rains in the afternoon. Unless you want to get lost, download the metro map. If you get tired, we'll take a cable car to see the view. You'll love it!

See you soon,
Andrés

9.title: What will happen if…?
9.brief: Choose a problem (traffic, pollution, too much screen time). Write about the consequences if people don't change.
9.briefEs: Elige un problema (tráfico, contaminación, pantallas) y escribe sus consecuencias si la gente no cambia.
criteria: Three first conditional sentences about consequences.
Use “as long as” once.
Use “consequence” and “to improve”.
9.model: Screen time is a big problem for children nowadays. If kids spend six hours a day on screens, they won't sleep well. If they don't play outside, they will have health problems. Another consequence is that they won't talk to their families. But the situation can improve. As long as parents set rules, children will use phones in a healthy way. If schools organise more sports, kids will be more active. We need to act now.

10.title: Things I love and hate
10.brief: Write about activities you enjoy and activities you can't stand. Explain why.
10.briefEs: Escribe sobre actividades que disfrutas y que no soportas, y explica por qué.
criteria: Five verbs followed by gerunds (enjoy, can’t stand, don’t mind, prefer, be into).
Three clauses with “because” and one with “because of”.
Use “fed up with” or “bored / boring”.
10.model: I really enjoy cooking for my friends because it relaxes me. I'm also into hiking: I go every weekend because of the fresh air. I don't mind washing the dishes, but I can't stand ironing clothes because it's so boring. I prefer listening to podcasts to watching TV. I'm fed up with waiting for the bus every morning, so I'm thinking of buying a bike. What about you?

10.title: Answer a friend's profile
10.brief: Reply to this post: “I love dancing. I don't like getting up early. I can't stand rainy days.” Agree or disagree with short responses and give reasons.
10.briefEs: Responde a un post diciendo si coincides o no con respuestas cortas y razones.
criteria: Short responses: So do I. / Neither do I. / I do. / I don’t.
Gerunds after like / love / can’t stand.
Two reasons with “because”.
10.model: Hi! I read your post. You love dancing? So do I! I take salsa classes because it's great exercise. You don't like getting up early? Neither do I. I'm a night person, so mornings are terrible for me. But I don't agree about rainy days. I love them because I can stay home, read and drink hot chocolate. Maybe we can go dancing one day — but not in the morning!

10.title: A review of a hobby class
10.brief: Write a review of a class or course you took (dance, cooking, yoga). Say what you enjoyed and didn't enjoy and why.
10.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una clase que tomaste: lo que disfrutaste, lo que no y por qué.
criteria: Four gerunds as objects (I enjoyed learning…).
Use “because” and “because of” correctly.
Use “to be worth it” and one -ed / -ing adjective pair.
10.model: I took a pottery class for six weeks at the community centre. I really enjoyed working with my hands because it was relaxing. I loved making my own cups. The teacher was patient and the classes were never boring. I didn't enjoy cleaning the room at the end, and I was sometimes bored because of the long explanations. But I don't mind getting dirty, so I had fun. The course was cheap and it was definitely worth it. I recommend it!

11.title: A famous invention
11.brief: Write a short text about a famous invention or building. Say who invented or built it, when, and how it is used today.
11.briefEs: Escribe un texto informativo sobre un invento o edificio famoso con la voz pasiva.
criteria: Three passive sentences in the past with “by” (was invented by).
Two passive sentences in the present (is used, are made).
Correct past participles (built, made, written).
11.model: The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876. The first call was made to his assistant, Thomas Watson. At first, the telephone was used only by rich people and businesses. Later, millions of phones were produced in factories around the world. Today, mobile phones are used by almost everyone. They are made in many countries, and they are used for calls, messages, photos and much more. Old telephones are now shown in museums.

11.title: How coffee is produced
11.brief: Describe how a Colombian product (coffee, chocolate, panela, flowers) is produced. Use the passive in the present.
11.briefEs: Describe cómo se produce un producto colombiano usando la voz pasiva en presente.
criteria: Six passive verbs in the present simple (is grown, are picked…).
Use sequence words: first, then, after that, finally.
Include “to be based on”, “to deliver” or “to carry out”.
11.model: Colombian coffee is famous all over the world. First, the coffee plants are grown on farms in the mountains. Then the red cherries are picked by hand. After that, the beans are washed and dried in the sun. Next, the beans are sorted and quality tests are carried out. The coffee is packed in big bags and it is delivered to ports. Finally, it is sold in many countries. Most of it is exported to the USA.

11.title: News: a robbery in my street
11.brief: Write a short news report about something that happened (a robbery, a fire, an accident). Focus on the action using the passive.
11.briefEs: Escribe una noticia corta sobre un suceso enfocándote en la acción con la voz pasiva.
criteria: Four passive verbs in the past (was stolen, were damaged).
Use “by” only when the agent is important.
A short title and one active sentence for contrast.
11.model:
BANK ROBBED IN CHAPINERO
A small bank was robbed yesterday morning in Chapinero. About 20 million pesos were stolen. Two windows were damaged and one employee was hurt, but not seriously. The robbers were seen by a taxi driver, who called the police. The area was closed for three hours. Two men were arrested last night. The police are still looking for the money.

12.title: When the lights went out
12.brief: Write a story about a time when something interrupted you (a blackout, a phone call, an earthquake). Use the past continuous and the simple past.
12.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre una interrupción usando pasado continuo y pasado simple.
criteria: Three past continuous verbs for background actions.
Two interruptions with “when” + simple past.
Use “suddenly” or “just then” and one word from the unit.
12.model: It was a stormy night. I was studying for a test and my sister was watching a horror film. My parents were cooking dinner. Suddenly, the lights went out. My sister screamed! While we were looking for candles, someone knocked on the door. We were so scared. Just then, my dad opened the door and it was our neighbour, Don Jorge. He was carrying a big lamp. We all laughed and had dinner together by candlelight.

12.title: What I've been doing lately
12.brief: Write an email to a friend telling him or her what you have been doing lately. Use the present perfect continuous.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo contándole qué has estado haciendo últimamente.
criteria: Four verbs in the present perfect continuous (have been working…).
Use “lately / recently” and “for / since”.
One sentence about how you feel (exhausted, excited).
12.model:
Hi Lina!

Sorry I haven't written. I've been working really hard lately. I've been helping my boss with a new project since January, so I'm exhausted. I've also been taking guitar lessons for two months. My neighbour hates it! And my brother has been staying with me because he's been looking for a flat. What have you been doing recently?

Hugs,
Ángela

12.title: A progress report
12.brief: Write a short report about a project you are still working on (a garden, a course, saving money). Say how long you have been doing it and what happened along the way.
12.briefEs: Escribe un informe corto sobre un proyecto en curso: desde cuándo lo haces y qué ha pasado.
criteria: Two present perfect continuous verbs with for / since.
One past continuous + simple past (I was planting when…).
Use “progress”, “to deal with” or “to keep an eye on”.
12.model:
Project: my vegetable garden
I have been growing vegetables on my balcony since March. I have been reading a lot about plants, and I have made good progress: I have tomatoes, lettuce and herbs now. Last month there was a problem. I was watering the plants when I saw small insects on the leaves. I dealt with them using a natural spray. Now I keep an eye on the plants every morning. I have been saving money because I don't buy vegetables any more!

13.title: A disappointing trip
13.brief: Write an email about a trip that was not as good as you expected. Use participle adjectives (-ing and -ed).
13.briefEs: Escribe un correo sobre un viaje decepcionante usando adjetivos terminados en -ing y -ed.
criteria: Three pairs or forms of -ing / -ed adjectives used correctly.
One relative clause with “who” and one with “which / that”.
Include “disappointing”, “exhausting” or “annoying”.
13.model:
Hi Paula,

I'm back from San Andrés and, honestly, the trip was disappointing. The flight was delayed for six hours, which was really annoying. When we arrived, we were exhausted. The hotel that we booked was far from the beach. The tour guide, who was very friendly, tried to help, but the weather was terrible: it rained every day! I was bored most of the time. The only fascinating thing was the colour of the sea.

Talk soon,
Majo

13.title: A person I admire
13.brief: Describe a person who has influenced you. Use relative pronouns to give information about them.
13.briefEs: Describe a una persona que te ha influido usando pronombres relativos (who, that, which, whose).
criteria: Four relative clauses with who, that, which or whose.
Two participle adjectives (inspiring, impressed).
Include “reliable” or “to come across as”.
13.model: The person who has influenced me most is my aunt Gloria. She is a doctor that works in a small hospital in Chocó. She is a woman whose patience is amazing. At first she comes across as serious, but she is very funny. Her work, which is often exhausting, is very inspiring for me. I was really impressed when she saved a baby's life during a storm. She is the most reliable person I know. I want to be like her.

13.title: Lost and found
13.brief: You lost something important. Write a notice for the building or school notice board describing the object.
13.briefEs: Escribe un aviso para el tablero describiendo algo importante que perdiste.
criteria: Two relative clauses (a bag which has…, the person who finds it).
Use “broken” or another past participle as an adjective.
Include contact information and a polite request.
13.model:
LOST: BLACK BACKPACK
I lost a black backpack which has a small broken zip on the front. It contains a laptop that has a sticker of a cat, and a blue notebook whose pages are full of notes for my thesis. I lost it on Monday in the library. The person who finds it will get a reward! Please call or write to Juan: 311 456 7890. Thank you!

14.title: Rules of my house
14.brief: Write the rules for living in your house or for a guest staying with you. Use modals of permission, obligation and prohibition.
14.briefEs: Escribe las reglas de tu casa para un huésped usando modales de permiso, obligación y prohibición.
criteria: Use can / be allowed to for permission.
Use have to / must for obligation and mustn’t / not allowed to for prohibition.
Use “be supposed to” once.
14.model: Welcome to our house! Here are the rules. You can use the kitchen any time, and you're allowed to invite friends on weekends. You have to wash your dishes after eating. You must close the main door at night because the cat escapes. You aren't allowed to smoke inside. You mustn't play loud music after 10 p.m. because the neighbours complain. You're supposed to tell us if you come home very late. Enjoy your stay!

14.title: Where's my phone?
14.brief: You can't find your phone. Write a message to a friend guessing where it is. Use modals and adverbs of certainty.
14.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo adivinando dónde está tu celular usando grados de certeza.
criteria: Use must, might, could and can’t for deduction.
Use two adverbs: probably, perhaps, definitely.
Include “evidence”, “to assume” or “unlikely”.
14.model: Hi Mafe, I can't find my phone! I'm writing from my laptop. It must be in your car, because I used it there last night. Or it might be in the restaurant. Perhaps I left it on the table. It can't be at home: I've looked everywhere! It's unlikely that someone took it. Can you check your car? I probably dropped it under the seat. Thanks!

14.title: Rules at my workplace
14.brief: Write an email to a friend comparing the rules at your work or school with the rules at his or hers.
14.briefEs: Escribe un correo comparando las reglas de tu trabajo o colegio con las de un amigo.
criteria: Four different modals of obligation / permission.
Use “prohibited” or “forbidden”.
One sentence of certainty (I'm sure / it's probably).
14.model:
Hi Juancho,

Your new job sounds strict! At my office the rules are more relaxed. We don't have to wear a suit — we're allowed to wear jeans every day. We can work from home on Fridays. But we have to arrive before 8:30, and phones are prohibited in meetings. We're supposed to have lunch in one hour, but nobody checks. At your company, are you allowed to work from home? It's probably difficult with so many rules!

Cheers,
Pipe

15.title: If I won the lottery
15.brief: Write about what you would do if you won a lot of money. Use the second conditional.
15.briefEs: Escribe qué harías si te ganaras la lotería usando el segundo condicional.
criteria: Five second conditional sentences (If + past, would + verb).
Use “If I were…” once.
Use “instead of” or “otherwise”.
15.model: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house for my parents first. Then I would travel around the world for a year. I would visit Japan, Egypt and Peru. If I had a lot of money, I wouldn't stop working, but I would start my own company instead of working for a boss. I would also help a school in my town. If I were a millionaire, I would be careful, otherwise I would lose everything!

15.title: A decision I regret
15.brief: Write about a decision you made in the past that you regret. Say what you should have done and what would have happened.
15.briefEs: Escribe sobre una decisión que lamentas: qué deberías haber hecho y qué habría pasado.
criteria: Two sentences with “should have / shouldn’t have + past participle”.
Two sentences with “would have + past participle”.
Use “to regret”, “to turn down” or “in hindsight”.
15.model: Three years ago, I was offered a job in Spain, but I turned it down because I was afraid. I regret it now. I should have accepted the offer. I shouldn't have listened to my fears. In hindsight, it would have been a great experience. I would have learned a lot and I would have met people from different countries. But I learned a lesson: next time I'll say yes to new opportunities, even if they scare me.

15.title: Advice in your shoes
15.brief: A friend wrote: “My boss is unfair and I want to quit, but I need the money.” Write a reply with advice using “If I were you…”.
15.briefEs: Responde a un amigo con un problema en el trabajo con consejos usando “If I were you…”.
criteria: Use “If I were you / In your shoes, I would…”.
Three second conditional sentences.
One past modal: should have or would have.
15.model:
Hi Jaime,

I'm sorry about your boss. If I were you, I wouldn't quit right now. In your shoes, I would look for another job first. If you talked to the HR department, they might help you. If I had a boss like that, I would write down every problem. Maybe you should have complained earlier, but it's not too late. Don't blame yourself!

Take care,
Silvia

16.title: What did they say?
16.brief: You went to a meeting and your colleague missed it. Write a message reporting what people said and asked.
16.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un colega que faltó a una reunión reportando lo que dijeron.
criteria: Four reported statements with backshift (said that she was…).
Two reported requests or commands (told us to…, asked us not to…).
Use “tell” with a person and “say” without.
16.model: Hi Andrés, you missed the meeting! The boss said that the company was opening a new office in Cali. She told us that sales were going up. Mario said he wanted to move to the new office. The boss asked us to send our reports by Friday. She also told us not to use the meeting room on Monday. Oh, and she said she would buy pizza for everyone next week!

16.title: A message from the doctor
16.brief: You went to the doctor. Write an email to a friend reporting what the doctor said and told you to do.
16.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo reportando lo que el médico te dijo y te pidió hacer.
criteria: Three reported statements (She said that I had…).
Three reported commands with told me to / not to.
Include “to insist”, “to remind” or “apparently”.
16.model:
Hi Nati,

I went to the doctor today because of my back. She said that I had a small problem with a muscle. Apparently, I sit too much at work. She told me to walk for thirty minutes every day and she told me not to carry heavy bags. She insisted that I needed to sleep more, too. She reminded me to take the pills after meals. She said I would feel better in a week.

Love,
Caro

16.title: The interview
16.brief: Write about a job interview (real or invented). Report the interviewer's questions, statements and your answers.
16.briefEs: Relata una entrevista de trabajo reportando las preguntas, afirmaciones y tus respuestas.
criteria: Two reported questions (She asked me where I lived / if I…).
Two reported statements and one reported command.
Use two reporting verbs: mention, admit, promise, point out.
16.model: Last week I had an interview at a travel agency. The manager asked me why I wanted the job. I told her that I loved travelling and helping people. She asked me if I spoke other languages. I admitted that my French wasn't very good. She pointed out that most clients spoke English, so it wasn't a problem. Then she told me to wait outside. After ten minutes, she said I could start on Monday. I promised I would work hard.
